Prealgebra · Lesson 11.1

Measuring Angles

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Geometry starts with the simplest objects. A single point. Two points joined make a segment. Extend it in one direction and you get a ray. Extend it in both directions and you get a line. Now let two rays start from the same point. The opening between them is an angle. In this lesson you will learn to name angles and to measure how far they open, in degrees.

Key idea
Angles, names, and degrees. An angle is the opening between two rays that start at the same point. That shared point is the vertex and the two rays are the sides. Name an angle with three letters, always keeping the vertex in the middle, so ∠ABC∠ABC is the angle at BB. The order of the outer two letters is free, so ∠ABC=∠CBA∠ABC=∠CBA, and when only one angle sits at a point you may just write ∠B∠B. We measure how far an angle opens in degrees. A full turn is 360∘360∘, a straight line is half of that at 180∘180∘, and a square corner, called a right angle, is 90∘90∘. A protractor reads the degrees directly. We sort angles by how far they open. An acute angle is below 90∘90∘, right is exactly 90∘90∘, obtuse is between 90∘90∘ and 180∘180∘, straight is exactly 180∘180∘, and reflex is more than 180∘180∘, measured the long way around.
Problem
In the diagram above, ∠ABC∠ABC is a right angle (the small square at BB marks it), and ray BXBX splits it into two parts. The diagram gives ∠XBC=28∘∠XBC=28∘. Find ∠ABX∠ABX. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The little square tells you ∠ABC∠ABC is a right angle, so the whole thing measures 90∘90∘.
  • Ray BXBX cuts that right angle into ∠ABX∠ABX and ∠XBC∠XBC, and those two parts add up to the full 90∘90∘. You know one part already.
Show the full solution
The small square means ∠ABC∠ABC is a right angle, so the two pieces ray BXBX makes must fill 90∘90∘. One piece is given, so the other is what's left over. ∠ABX=90∘−28∘=62∠ABX=90∘−28∘=62​
Problem
In the diagram above, AA, OO, BB lie on a straight line and ray OCOC stands on it. The diagram gives ∠AOC=124∘∠AOC=124∘. Find ∠BOC∠BOC. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • ∠AOC∠AOC and ∠BOC∠BOC sit side by side along the straight line ABAB, so together they form a straight angle. How many degrees is a straight angle?
  • A straight angle is 180∘180∘. Subtract the part you already know from 180180 to get the part you want.
Show the full solution
∠AOC∠AOC and ∠BOC∠BOC sit side by side along the straight line ABAB, so together they make a straight angle of 180∘180∘. ∠BOC=180−124=56∠BOC=180−124=56​
Problem
In the diagram above, ray OBOB lies inside ∠AOC∠AOC, and ∠AOB=88∘∠AOB=88∘. The whole angle ∠AOC=147∘∠AOC=147∘. What is ∠BOC∠BOC? Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • Ray OBOB cuts the big angle into two pieces, and those two pieces add up to the whole ∠AOC∠AOC.
  • You know the whole angle and one piece, so ∠BOC∠BOC is what is left over. Subtract.
Show the full solution
The two parts ∠AOB∠AOB and ∠BOC∠BOC add up to the whole angle ∠AOC∠AOC. So ∠BOC∠BOC is the whole minus the part you already know. ∠BOC=147∘−88∘=59∠BOC=147∘−88∘=59​
Key idea
Adjacent angles add. Two angles are adjacent when they share a vertex and a side. If a ray splits a larger angle into two adjacent parts, they add to the whole, so ∠AOB+∠BOC=∠AOC∠AOB+∠BOC=∠AOC. Add the two smaller angles to get the larger one, or subtract a known part from the whole to find the other part.
Problem
In the diagram above, ∠AOC∠AOC is a right angle and ray ODOD splits it. Given that ∠AOD=37∘∠AOD=37∘, find ∠DOC∠DOC. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A right angle measures 90∘90∘, and ray ODOD breaks it into the two pieces ∠AOD∠AOD and ∠DOC∠DOC.
  • Those two pieces together make the whole right angle, so ∠AOD+∠DOC=90∘∠AOD+∠DOC=90∘. Subtract to find the missing piece.
Show the full solution
Ray ODOD splits the right angle ∠AOC∠AOC into two parts that add to 90∘90∘. The two angles are complementary, so ∠DOC=90−37=53.∠DOC=90−37=53​.
Problem
In the diagram above, two rays make an angle of 110∘110∘, and the question mark marks the reflex angle, the big way around the outside. What is the reflex angle? Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A full turn all the way around a point is 360∘360∘. The reflex angle and the 110∘110∘ angle together sweep out that whole turn.
  • So the reflex angle is what is left after you take the 110∘110∘ away from 360∘360∘.
Show the full solution
The 110∘110∘ angle and the reflex angle together sweep the full turn around the vertex, which is 360∘360∘. 360∘−110∘=250360∘−110∘=250​ An angle and the reflex angle beside it always pair up to 360∘360∘, so either one hands you the other.
Problem
In the diagram above, ray OQOQ bisects ∠POR∠POR, so the equal tick marks show the two halves are equal. Given that one half ∠POQ=41∘∠POQ=41∘, what is the whole ∠POR∠POR? Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A bisector cuts an angle into two equal halves, so ∠POR∠POR is made of two copies of ∠POQ∠POQ.
  • The whole is twice one half. Double 41∘41∘.
Show the full solution
A bisector splits an angle into two equal halves, so the whole is twice one half. ∠POR=2×41∘=82∘∠POR=2×41∘=82​∘
Key idea
Angle pairs and bisectors. Two angles are complementary when they add to 90∘90∘, forming a right angle. They are supplementary when they add to 180∘180∘, forming a straight line. Two angles side by side on a straight line form a linear pair, and a linear pair is always supplementary, so each angle is 180∘180∘ minus the other. A bisector is a ray from the vertex that splits an angle into two equal parts, so each part is half the whole. Equal tick marks on the two parts show that a ray bisects the angle.
Problem
In the diagram above, two straight lines cross at a point, forming four angles. One of them measures 74∘74∘, and the angle marked with the question mark sits directly across from it. What is the marked angle? Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The two marked angles are directly across the crossing point from each other. What is that pair of angles called?
  • Vertical angles, the pair sitting opposite each other where two lines cross, are always equal. So the marked angle matches the 74∘74∘ one.
Show the full solution
The marked angle sits directly across the crossing point from the 74∘74∘ angle, so the two are vertical angles and have the same measure. The marked angle is 7474​ degrees. Vertical angles match because each one shares a straight line with the same neighbor, so both come out as 180∘180∘ minus that neighbor.
Problem
In the diagram above, three rays leave a single point, cutting the whole way around into three angles. Two of them measure 137∘137∘ and 95∘95∘. Find the third angle, the one marked with the question mark. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • Going all the way around a point is one full turn, and a full turn is 360∘360∘. The three angles have to add up to that.
  • So the missing angle is what's left after you take the two known ones away from 360∘360∘.
Show the full solution
The three angles wrap all the way around the point, so they add to a full turn of 360∘360∘. Subtract the two you know. 360−137−95=128360−137−95=128​
Key idea
Around a point. When two straight lines cross they make four angles. Two angles directly across from each other are vertical angles, and they are always equal. Each is also supplementary to its neighbour, so one known angle gives all four. More generally, when angles meet around a single point with no gaps or overlaps, they fill one full turn, so they add to 360∘360∘. Know all but one and the last is 360∘360∘ minus the rest.
Fun fact
Why does a full circle have exactly 360∘360∘? The choice traces back to the ancient Babylonians, who counted in base 60 rather than base 10. The number 360 fit neatly in that system, and it lands close to the number of days in a year, so as the sun crept around the sky it moved almost one degree each day. Best of all, 360 divides evenly by a huge crowd of numbers, including 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, and 12. That made splitting a circle into equal parts easy, and thousands of years later we still measure angles their way.
Problem
In the diagram above, a ray splits the right angle ∠ABC∠ABC into two parts whose measures are in the ratio 1:51:5. Find the smaller part, the one marked with the question mark. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A right angle is 90∘90∘, and the two parts together make up that whole 90∘90∘.
  • A ratio of 1:51:5 means the angle is cut into 1+5=61+5=6 equal shares. The smaller part is just one of those shares.
Show the full solution
The ratio 1:51:5 splits the right angle into 1+5=61+5=6 equal shares. Since a right angle is 90∘90∘, each share is 90∘6=15∘.690∘​=15∘. The smaller part is one share, so it measures 1515​ degrees.
Problem
The clock in the diagram above shows 5:00. Find the measure of the (non-reflex) angle between the hour hand and the minute hand. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The 12 hour marks split the full 360∘360∘ evenly. How many degrees is one gap between neighboring marks?
  • Count how many of those gaps sit between the two hands at 5:00, then add up that many equal pieces.
Show the full solution
The 12 marks divide the full circle evenly, so each gap is 360∘12=30∘12360∘​=30∘. At 5:00 the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 5, which is 5 gaps away. So the angle is 5×30∘=1505×30∘=150​ degrees.
Problem
In the diagram above, a ray stands on a straight line, and the two angles it forms are labeled x∘x∘ and (x+10)∘(x+10)∘. Find xx. Give the number of degrees (the value of xx).
Show a hint
  • The ray sits on a straight line, so the two angles together open up all the way across it. What does a straight angle measure?
  • The two labeled angles are supplementary, so they add to 180∘180∘. Set up x+(x+10)=180x+(x+10)=180 and solve for xx.
Show the full solution
A ray standing on a straight line makes two supplementary angles, so they add to 180∘180∘. Adding the labels gives x+(x+10)=180,x+(x+10)=180, which simplifies to 2x+10=1802x+10=180. Then 2x=1702x=170, so x=85x=85​.
Problem
In the diagram above, two rays split the straight angle into three angles whose measures are in the ratio 2:3:42:3:4. Find the largest of the three, the one marked with the question mark. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A straight angle measures 180∘180∘, and the three parts together fill it. Think of the ratio 2:3:42:3:4 as splitting that 180∘180∘ into equal shares.
  • Add the ratio numbers: 2+3+4=92+3+4=9. So 180∘180∘ is cut into 99 equal shares. The largest angle takes 44 of them.
Show the full solution
The three angles sit along a straight line, so they add to 180∘180∘. The ratio 2:3:42:3:4 cuts that into 2+3+4=92+3+4=9 equal shares, so each share is 180∘9=20∘9180∘​=20∘. The largest angle is 44 shares. 49×180∘=4×20∘=8094​×180∘=4×20∘=80​
Problem
In the diagram above, an angle x∘x∘ and its supplement (180−x)∘(180−x)∘ sit side by side on a straight line. The angle is 15∘15∘ more than twice its supplement. Find the angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • Two angles that sit together on a straight line are supplementary, so they add to 180∘180∘. That is why the supplement is written (180−x)∘(180−x)∘.
  • Turn the words into an equation. "15∘15∘ more than twice its supplement" means x=2(180−x)+15x=2(180−x)+15. Expand the right side and collect the xx terms.
Show the full solution
The two angles sit together on a straight line, so the supplement of x∘x∘ is (180−x)∘(180−x)∘. The angle is 15∘15∘ more than twice that, so x=2(180−x)+15.x=2(180−x)+15. Expanding gives x=360−2x+15x=360−2x+15, so 3x=3753x=375 and x=125x=125​.

Practice these ideas

Practice
In the diagram above, ∠ABC∠ABC is a right angle and ray BXBX splits it into two smaller angles. Given that ∠XBC=34∘∠XBC=34∘, what is ∠ABX∠ABX? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The two pieces sit side by side and fill the right angle, so they add to 90∘90∘. That means ∠ABX∠ABX is whatever is left after taking away ∠XBC∠XBC. ∠ABX=90∘−34∘=56∠ABX=90∘−34∘=56​
Practice
In the diagram above, ray OBOB lies inside ∠AOC∠AOC, splitting it into two smaller angles. The diagram shows ∠AOB=92∘∠AOB=92∘, and the whole ∠AOC=155∘∠AOC=155∘. What is ∠BOC∠BOC? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
∠AOB∠AOB and ∠BOC∠BOC are the two pieces of ∠AOC∠AOC, so the missing piece is the whole minus the part you know. ∠BOC=155∘−92∘=63∠BOC=155∘−92∘=63​
Practice
In the diagram above, AOBAOB is a straight line and ray OCOC rises from point OO. Given that ∠AOC=113∘∠AOC=113∘, what is ∠BOC∠BOC? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
Angles on a straight line add up to 180∘180∘. Since ∠AOC∠AOC and ∠BOC∠BOC together form the straight line AOBAOB, ∠BOC=180∘−113∘=67∘.∠BOC=180∘−113∘=67​∘.
Practice
In the diagram above, ∠AOC∠AOC is a right angle and ray ODOD falls inside it. Given that ∠AOD=29∘∠AOD=29∘, what is ∠DOC∠DOC? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The two smaller angles sit inside the right angle and add up to it, so ∠AOD+∠DOC=90∘∠AOD+∠DOC=90∘. Subtract the part you know. ∠DOC=90∘−29∘=61∠DOC=90∘−29∘=61​
Practice
In the diagram above, ray OQOQ bisects ∠POR∠POR, so the two halves are equal. Given that ∠POQ=38∘∠POQ=38∘, what is the whole ∠POR∠POR? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
A bisector cuts an angle into two equal halves, so the whole is twice one half. ∠POR=2×38∘=76∠POR=2×38∘=76​
Practice
In the diagram above, two lines cross and one of the four angles measures 116∘116∘. The marked angle sits right beside it along the same straight line. What is the measure of the marked angle? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The marked angle and the 116∘116∘ angle sit side by side along a straight line, so they add to 180∘180∘. 180∘−116∘=64180∘−116∘=64​ Where two lines cross, every angle is either equal to a given one or supplementary to it.
Practice
In the diagram above, three rays from a single point split the space all the way around into three angles. Two of them measure 88∘88∘ and 145∘145∘. What is the third angle? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The three angles fill a complete turn around the point, so they add to 360∘360∘. Subtract the two you know. 360−88−145=127360−88−145=127​
Practice
In the diagram above, two rays open up to make an angle of 145∘145∘. The question mark marks the reflex angle, the one that sweeps all the way around the outside. What is the reflex angle? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The two angles at the vertex fill one complete turn, so together they add to 360∘360∘. Subtract the part you know from the whole turn. 360∘−145∘=215∘360∘−145∘=215​∘
Practice
In the diagram above, ray OPOP stands on a straight line, splitting the straight angle into x∘x∘ and 2x∘2x∘. Find xx. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The two angles rest on a straight line, so together they form a straight angle of 180∘180∘. Adding the pieces gives x+2x=3x=180,x+2x=3x=180, so x=60x=60​.
Practice
In the diagram above, ray BXBX splits the right angle ∠ABC∠ABC into two parts whose measures are in the ratio 2:72:7. What is the measure of the smaller part? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The ratio 2:72:7 cuts the right angle into 2+7=92+7=9 equal shares, so each share is 90∘÷9=10∘90∘÷9=10∘. The smaller part is 22 shares. 29×90∘=2092​×90∘=20​
Practice
In the diagram above, the angle y∘y∘ and its complement (90−y)∘(90−y)∘ together fill a right angle. The angle exceeds its complement by 40∘40∘. What is yy? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The angle is 40∘40∘ more than its complement, so y=(90−y)+40.y=(90−y)+40. The right side is 130−y130−y, so 2y=1302y=130 and y=65y=65​. The complement is then 25∘25∘, and 65−25=4065−25=40 checks out.
Practice
The clock in the diagram above reads 3:00. What is the non-reflex angle between the hour hand and the minute hand? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The clock face is a full turn of 360∘360∘ divided into 12 equal hour steps, so each step is 360∘÷12=30∘360∘÷12=30∘. At 3:00 the hour hand points at 3 and the minute hand points at 12, which are 3 steps apart. So the angle is 3×30∘=90∘3×30∘=90​∘.
Practice
In the diagram above, three rays from a single point split the full turn around that point into three angles whose measures are in the ratio 3:4:53:4:5. What is the measure of the largest of these three angles? Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The three angles go all the way around the point, so they add to a full turn of 360∘360∘. The ratio 3:4:53:4:5 splits that turn into 3+4+5=123+4+5=12 equal shares, so one share is 360∘12=30∘12360∘​=30∘. The largest angle is 55 shares. 5×30∘=512×360∘=1505×30∘=125​×360∘=150​
